plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, PLTU) to zero.
Sell METU to reduce high-beta software risk.
Trim QQQI to 20% to reduce income concentration.
Trim SPY to 15% to reduce broad index exposure.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation with reduced leverage.
Expect lower volatility and a more conservative return profile.
conservative.read: This plan aims for capital preservation with a target of ~1.5% per month. It significantly reduces leverage and focuses on lower-risk assets, aiming for low drawdowns. However, growth potential is also limited.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, PLTU) to low single digits.
Trim METU to reduce high-beta software risk.
Trim QQQI to 20% and SPY to 15% to rebalance.
Buy XLV to add defensive sector exposure.
This plan balances risk reduction with growth opportunities.
Expect moderate returns with controlled drawdowns.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets ~2.5% per month by reducing leverage and concentration while adding a defensive sector. It seeks risk-first growth, aiming for a blend of stability and upside potential. Drawdowns are expected to be manageable.

plan: Increase leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, PLTU) and METU.
Trim QQQI to 15% and SPY to 10% to free up capital.
Buy SQQQ to add a short-term hedge.
This plan aggressively pursues growth through leverage and concentration.
Expect higher potential returns but also significantly larger drawdowns.
Strict stop discipline is crucial due to amplified risk and ETF decay.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4% per month by increasing leverage and concentrating in high-beta assets, including leveraged ETFs. It accepts significantly higher risk and potential drawdowns. Daily rebalancing of leveraged ETFs can impact performance, and strict stop discipline is essential.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, PLTU) and high-beta software (METU, CRWD, SNOW).
Increase QQQI to 30% to maximize income generation.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly income over growth.
It aims for low drawdowns by reducing volatile assets.
Expect consistent distributions, but NAV can still decline in market downturns.
This is a strategy for generating income, not aggressive capital appreciation.
income.read: This income-focused plan targets ~1% per month through distributions from income-oriented ETFs like QQQI. It minimizes leverage and volatile single stocks to prioritize capital preservation and steady cash flow. While aiming for low drawdowns, the Net Asset Value can still decrease during market selloffs.
